newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU split on beef labelling.
newsitem.headline: EU split on beef labelling.

text.p: A European Commission plan to make beef labelling compulsory has run into strong opposition from European Union member states and may be blocked at next week's farm Council, an EU diplomat said on Wednesday.

The Commission presented a revised proposal to the EU special agriculture committee on Monday, changing its original proposal for a voluntary system aimed at restoring consumer confidence in beef following the mad cow crisis.

The new proposal seeks to change the legal proceedure used to adopt legislation from Article 43, which allows the Council of Ministers to decide following a European Parliament opinion, to a co-decision procedure requiring both to agree.
The move followed a pledge Commission President Jacques Santer gave the parliament last month.

Responding to a debate on the outcome of the parliament's Temporary Committee of Inquiry into BSE (Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy) Santer said he believed all veterinary, phyto-sanitary and some other agricultural legislation should be by co-decision with the parliament in future.

"The Commission's proposal on labelling was presented on Monday and it is radically different from the original proposal. Where the original proposed a voluntary arrangement the new one includes compulsory items that meat must be labelled with," the diplomat said.
The new proposal includes a requirement for beef to be labelled with the country of origin.
The committee discussion is said to have "moved backwards" over the new Article 100a proposal with a blocking minority of member states rejecting a compulsory labelling system.
Both the new proposal and the original redrafted to include compromise changes put forward by the Dutch EU presidency will now be put to next week's Council, the diplomat said.
"It will be for ministers to decide which proposal and which legal base (proceedure) to go with," the diplomat commented.
Progress was made on a related animal identification proposal which, apart from some technical issues, was agreed by the committee of member state officials, the diplomat added.
The Dutch Presidency will put a third Commission proposal for financing the beef measures to ministers as part of the same package but it is not controversial, the diplomat added.
